title: MRIs of UFO-contact DoD and intelligence personnel show enlarged caudate-putamen region
summary: Garry Nolan tells of MRIs of UFO-contact DoD and intelligence personnel show enlarged caudate-putamen region, about c. 2010s at Stanford University, California, and says they saw it or took part. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: And then they showed me MRIs of some of these people and most of those people had interactions with UFOs and these were Department of Defense and intelligence people.
But if we find out that a disproportionate amount of fighter pilots who see UFOs have an enlarged caudate nucleus and putamen.
tellings.difference: The host tells it second-hand and as a hypothetical about fighter pilots who see UFOs being disproportionately affected, where Nolan describes MRIs of DoD and intelligence personnel he was shown.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of Garry Nolan's Stanford brain-imaging finding that people who had UFO encounters show an enlarged caudate nucleus and putamen. The host is retelling Nolan's finding, and Nolan tells it first-hand in the story.

as_told.title: Nolan's brain findings in pilots who see UFOs

tellings.quote: in looking at the MRIs of some of these people we noticed a area of the brain that seemed to be disturbed let's say or different in many of these individuals
tellings.difference: Puts it more cautiously, calling the area 'disturbed or different' rather than enlarged, and does not mention DoD or intelligence personnel.
tellings.link_reason: Both are Garry Nolan's own account of MRIs of UFO-contact people at Stanford showing a different caudate-putamen region.

as_told.title: Garry Nolan's MRI findings on the caudate-putamen and intuition

plain: Garry Nolan, a scientist at Stanford University, says that in the 2010s he was shown MRIs, which are detailed brain scans, of people from the Department of Defense (the US military) and intelligence agencies, most of whom had had run-ins with UFOs, and that they showed a larger than usual caudate-putamen, a pair of structures deep in the brain. If true, it could mean some people are wired in a way that makes these encounters more likely. The podcast host Jesse Michels later raised it as a question, wondering whether fighter pilots who see UFOs might more often have this brain feature.
